_comment: Prospecting-potential composite — per-commodity config (docs/briefs/TIER_B_FABLE_BRIEF.md; PROJECT_PLAN §5.3, decisions #41/#42). THE generic core: adding a commodity = a new entry here + its MRDS producer pull (see second_commodity_stub). Read by scripts/etl/build_prospectivity.sql (loaded into PG as jsonb) and by the frontend (strings + labels). Thresholds are percentile fractions [0..1]; distances in meters. method_filters values are case-insensitive SQL LIKE patterns against tbl_chem.analytic_method — an element listed there only counts when its method matches (Au: INAA / fire-assay only, because standard ICP detection limits sit far above stream-sediment gold levels — the 'Au is censored' spike finding).

commodities.label: Gold
commodities._method_filters_note: Verified against the release 2026-07-10: the actual analytic_method codes are abbreviated (FA_*=fire assay, NA_*=neutron activation/INAA, AA_*_HBr=HBr-extraction atomic absorption, MS_*=ICP-MS — all dedicated low-detection-limit Au methods). This widens the brief's literal 'INAA/fire-assay' wording to match its SUBSTANCE (exclude high-DL emission-spec packages: AES_*/ES_* and non-extraction AA are NOT matched). AA_F_HBr alone carries 48,560 of the ~176k detected Au values nationally.

producer_source.note: gold-filtered pull (pull_mrds.sh); a later commodity needs its own commodity-filtered MRDS pull

strings.pathfinder_blurb: Why As/Sb/Ag? These elements travel with gold in the same ore-forming fluids and are measurable at trace levels where gold itself hides below lab detection limits — elevated together, they mark gold-style chemistry.
strings.chemistry_earned: Earned by chemistry alone — no recorded historic producer nearby (historic records are incomplete).
strings.upstream_note: Signal detected in this drainage — the source may be anywhere upstream of this point. Explore the drainage above; this is a lead, not a dig-here.
strings.vintage_note: USGS NGDB geochemistry (samples 1962–2023, 2026 release) + historic MRDS records.
